era_setting.place: Texas, February 2021 -- Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio and the small towns between them; the ERCOT control room in Taylor, Texas; gas wellheads and compressor stations in the Permian Basin; the Texas Capitol in Austin for the 2021 legislative session
era_setting.notes: The film runs from the February 2011 FERC/NERC cold-weather report to the Texas Supreme Court's 2023 ruling on the pricing orders, and its centre of gravity is 14-19 February 2021. THIS IS A CONTEMPORARY SETTING and that is the whole reason it was chosen: 93.5% of the shelf's playable clips are modern stock, and this episode's register -- suburban American streets, ordinary interiors, power lines, snow on unprepared infrastructure, supermarket shelves, a car idling -- sits in the shelf's strongest half. Compare EP72, set in 2013, which had the same advantage, and the four period candidates rejected on 2026-08-21 for not having it. WHAT IS WRONG HERE IS NOT THE DECADE BUT THE PLACE AND THE WEATHER'S CHARACTER. OUT OF PLACE, and wrong in any cut: European or Asian streets and signage; EU number plates; right-hand-drive traffic; alpine or Nordic snow scenes -- deep snowbanks, ski resorts, pine forests under metres of snow, frozen lakes, aurora. Texas in Uri was a THIN, WRONG snow: two to six inches on ground that has no plough, ice on palms and live oaks, snow on a strip-mall car park, frozen fountains in a warm-climate town. Also wrong: New York, Chicago or any recognisably northern American city that handles snow routinely. OUT OF PERIOD: pre-2010 vehicles as the ordinary traffic, CRT televisions, flip phones. Declared because a snow query returns Scandinavia by default and this film is about a place that had never needed to be ready.

forbidden_claims: That winterization was legally required of Texas generators before 2021. It was recommended after the 2011 event and NERC declined to make it a standard; the requirement came afterwards, in 2021 legislation.
That any named individual or company caused the deaths. The film describes a system, a regulator that declined a standard, and a market design -- never a culprit.

A death toll other than the state's own final figure of 246, unless the alternative is attributed to the outlet or study that produced it and labelled as an estimate. The 246 figure is the sixth and final report of the Texas Department of State Health Services.

That the grid 'collapsed'. It did not. Load was shed to prevent a collapse, and the margin is a measured number: frequency below 59.4 Hz for four minutes and twenty-three seconds against a nine-minute threshold.
That renewables or any single fuel caused the shortfall. The record attributes freeze-related outages across fuel types and to gas supply as well as generation.
Any figure for deaths, megawatts, prices, bills or duration that is not in the FACTS_LEDGER with a source.
Any characterisation of an identifiable Texan's household, bill or bereavement that is not sourced and attributed.
notes: Runtime band matches EP72 at the owner's instruction that EP73-76 are all 30 minutes. script_words is set HIGHER than EP72's [4600,4800] on measurement: EP72's narration delivered at 191.7 wpm end-to-end for a script of short declaratives, so 5,276 words produced a 1,774.8 s master. This episode is written in the same register; 4,900-5,400 words is the band that lands 29:00-32:00 at that measured pace. Re-derive from `gen_narration_case.py --measure-section ACT_1` before writing to length -- the model rate of 171.79 wpm in the narration registry is 11% slow for this register and sizing to it produced a script four minutes short on EP72. people_plates_min raised from 20 to 24: the owner's decision of 2026-08-21 is that faces are wanted, and this episode's people are ordinary Texans with no real individual behind them, so the people lane can carry more here than it could in EP72. R2: no named victim is depicted; the deaths are real and recent.
